## Requirements

- **Delphi 12+ (Athens)** — required for multi-line string literals (`'''`), which five shipped units use
- **Windows** — Win32 and Win64. No package declares a Linux target

## Installation

DAF is distributed as source: a set of Delphi packages (`.dpk`). Every release on GitHub carries it
as a zip, **Source code (zip)** under the release's *Assets*:
<https://github.com/Delphi-DAF/dafce/releases>. Unzip it anywhere, a path with spaces included, and
run everything below from that folder. Or clone the repo:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Delphi-DAF/dafce.git
```

### Building the packages

Every project takes its output paths from `src/paths.optset`, which derives all of them from
`PRJ_OUT_DIR`. `BDS.bat` sets that variable from its own location, so the IDE is started through it:

```cmd
BDS start
```

That opens RAD Studio with the project's environment and loads `src/DAFGroup.groupproj`. An IDE
started any other way leaves `PRJ_OUT_DIR` undefined, and every output path is then built from an
empty value. `BDS inspect` prints what is set; the project's own variables live in `project.cmd`,
and per-machine overrides go in a `%COMPUTERNAME%.project.cmd` beside it.

`BDS.bat` keeps each folder's IDE profile under `HKCU\Software\Embarcadero\DAF\<folder name>`.
Deleting the folder leaves that key behind, and
`reg delete "HKCU\Software\Embarcadero\DAF\<folder name>" /f` removes it.

From the command line there is nothing to set up — both scripts call `BDS.bat` themselves:

```cmd
buildall.bat all
runtests.bat all
```

With no options, `buildall.bat` builds the framework in Debug and Release, then the samples and the
specs in Debug. These options build only part of it, and they combine:

| Option | Builds |
|---|---|
| `--framework` | the framework, in Debug and Release |
| `--samples` | the framework in Debug, then the samples |
| `--specs` | the framework in Debug, then the specs |

`runtests.bat` runs every suite the specs group declares. Both take `Win32`, `Win64` or `all`, and
`buildall.bat` also takes `--clean`, which deletes `out/` first.

### Choosing the Delphi version

`project.cmd` selects Delphi 13 (`PRJ_IDE=D370`). Delphi 12 is `PRJ_IDE=D290`, and either of these
selects it without editing `project.cmd`:

- a `%COMPUTERNAME%.project.cmd` next to `project.cmd`, holding the line `set "PRJ_IDE=D290"`;
- `set "PRJ_IDE=D290"` on its own line in the console, before running `buildall.bat`.

With Delphi 12, `buildall.bat --framework --samples` builds the framework and the samples. The
specs of the VCL module need Delphi 13, so `--specs`, and `buildall.bat` with no options, end in
`BUILD FAILED`.

When the version asked for is not installed, `BDS.bat` builds nothing, exits with code 2 and lists
the installed versions with the `PRJ_IDE` of each.

### Using what is built

Add `out\Win32\Release\lib` or `out\Win64\Release\lib` to your project's search path, and the DAF
units your program uses compile against it. `out\<Platform>\Debug\lib` holds the Debug build of the
same units, for debugging.

### Using the source directly

Adding the `src/[Module]/` paths you need to your own project's search path compiles those units with
your project's output paths, so none of the above applies. Every module is self-contained.

## Your first DAF application

This is the `QuickStart` sample, verbatim — it is the file the compiler reads, and a check
compares the two, so what you copy from here is what builds:

<!-- quickstart: src/Cli/samples/QuickStart/QuickStart.dpr -->

```pascal
program QuickStart;

{$APPTYPE CONSOLE}

uses
  Daf.Extensions.DependencyInjection,
  Daf.CommandLine,
  Daf.Configuration.CommandLine,
  Daf.Cli;

// El ejemplo de entrada de una herramienta de linea de comandos: el builder, la accion de la raiz
// escrita en el sitio, los argumentos que recibe la gramatica, y el codigo de salida que devuelve
// esa accion.
//
//   QuickStart         -> 0, saluda
//   QuickStart --help  -> 0, la ayuda
//
// Como se anade un servicio esta en el sample ServiceWiring, que es el nivel siguiente.
begin
  var B := TCliApplication.CreateBuilder(CommandLineConfig.ProcessArgs);

  B.SetAction(
    function(const Services: IServiceProvider; const Parsed: IParseResult): Integer
    begin
      Writeln('Hola desde DAF');
      Result := TCliExit.Ok;
    end);

  B.ParseArgs(CommandLineConfig.ProcessArgs);
  ExitCode := B.Build.Run;
end.
```

Three things about the shape, all of them easy to get wrong:

- The builder is held in a variable, not chained, and registration happens where it is written:
  there is no deferred `ConfigureServices` callback. `TCliApplication.CreateBuilder` returns an
  `ICliApplicationBuilder`, whose `Build` returns the `ICliApplication` whose `Run` is the exit code.
- The arguments go to two calls, and each one feeds one reader: `CreateBuilder` adds them to the
  configuration, and `ParseArgs` hands them to the grammar, which answers `--help` with no option
  declared. Without `ParseArgs`, the grammar parses an empty invocation.
- `Daf.Extensions.DependencyInjection` is in the `uses` although nothing is registered: the
  signature of the action names `IServiceProvider`, and Delphi needs the type visible to write it.

## Adding a service

The `ServiceWiring` sample is the same program with one service registered and resolved:

<!-- quickstart: src/Cli/samples/ServiceWiring/ServiceWiring.dpr -->

```pascal
program ServiceWiring;

{$APPTYPE CONSOLE}
{$STRONGLINKTYPES ON}

uses
  System.SysUtils,
  Daf.Extensions.DependencyInjection,
  Daf.CommandLine,
  Daf.Configuration.CommandLine,
  Daf.Cli,
  ServiceWiring.Greeter in 'ServiceWiring.Greeter.pas';

// Como entra un servicio en una herramienta de linea de comandos: se registra en el builder, que
// ya esta vivo, y la accion lo resuelve del proveedor que recibe.
//
//   ServiceWiring  -> 0, saluda a traves del servicio
begin
  var B := TCliApplication.CreateBuilder(CommandLineConfig.ProcessArgs);

  B.Services.AddSingleton<IGreeter, TGreeter>;

  B.SetAction(
    function(const Services: IServiceProvider; const Parsed: IParseResult): Integer
    begin
      Writeln(Services.GetRequiredService<IGreeter>.Greet);
      Result := TCliExit.Ok;
    end);

  B.ParseArgs(CommandLineConfig.ProcessArgs);
  ExitCode := B.Build.Run;
end.
```

- `Services` answers before anything is built, so `AddSingleton` takes effect where it is written,
  and the action declared with `SetAction` resolves from the provider it receives.
- The service lives in its own unit. A type declared in the `.dpr` is not in the `interface`
  section of any unit, and resolving it fails at run time with `ENonPublicType`. That is also why
  the program carries `{$STRONGLINKTYPES ON}`: without it the linker drops the RTTI the container
  resolves by.

There is a second, lower-level entry point — `THostBuilder` from the **Hosting** module — for when
you want the host without the application layer around it, with
[`Hosting/samples/HostQuickStart`](https://github.com/Delphi-DAF/dafce/tree/main/src/Hosting/samples/HostQuickStart)
as its own entry example. The
[Application guide](../modules/application-guide.qmd) says what each one gives you.

## Module map

| If you need… | Use module |
|---|---|
| DI container | [DependencyInjection](../modules/di.qmd) |
| App lifecycle | [Hosting](../modules/hosting.qmd) |
| Config files / env vars | [Configuration](../modules/configuration.qmd) |
| Structured logging | [Logging](../modules/logging.qmd) |
| Commands / queries | [MediatR](../modules/mediator.qmd) |
| BDD specs / tests | [MiniSpec](../modules/minispec.qmd) |
| NLog-style logging | [NNLog](../modules/nnlog.qmd) |
| Smart pointers / RTTI | [Commons](../modules/commons.qmd) |
| HTTP server / routing | [Web](../modules/web.qmd) |
